out.other_title: Definition of the two-agent debate game (answers, alternating statements, judge)
out.rationale: Irving et al. define a debate game where two agents state answers, alternate statements and a judge picks the winner. Michael et al. define an information-asymmetric debate where the judge states prior credences, interjects between turns, ends the debate when ready, and debaters can include certified verbatim quotes up to l_q characters per turn; these additions change the game from fixed alternation to judge-controlled interaction.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: two-debater debate protocols judged by a weaker party, extended with judge interaction and certified evidence

text: The authors define debates as turn-based textual exchanges between a judge and debaters A and B randomly assigned to two answers, one correct: the judge states prior credences, both debaters give simultaneous opening statements, then the judge, A and B take turns until the judge ends the debate. Each debater turn has up to l_c characters, of which up to l_q may be certified verbatim quotes from the story, highlighted as ground-truth evidence.
